confirmed_design: Item is the common root for several item branches and intermediate/child types.
The equipment branch is Item -> Equipment -> Gear.
Gear includes weapons, armour/clothing, trinkets and other wearable or wieldable equipment. Do not name the common gear branch Clothing.
Food and potions belong to non-equipment item branches. They must not inherit equipment slot or worn-gear stat behavior merely because they are inventory items.
Preserve intermediate types and concrete child definitions where original evidence establishes them; the exact complete original tree has not yet been recovered.
local_implementation_evidence: UFood_ItemObject currently derives directly from UItemObject and contains no food-specific effect implementation.
UEquipment_ItemObject currently derives from UItemObject. The user-confirmed Gear layer still needs implementation.
UItemBlueprint derives from UItemObject and represents a crafting recipe item with required-item and output references.
The reconstructed BP_GoldItem and BP_BronzeItem derive from ItemObject.
No potion-specific native class or potion item Blueprint was found in the inspected Source/DuTraveller and Content/Blueprints trees.
restoration_requirements: Shared identity, quantity, stack handling, inventory ownership, display metadata and replication belong to appropriate shared item layers.
Equipment and gear extend shared items with their actual equip/slot/appearance/stat rules; they do not absorb all inventory item types.
Food/potion use must validate eligibility and apply the intended server-side effect before consuming quantity. Failed use preserves the item.
Consumable effects must remain distinct from permanent attribute investment and worn-equipment modifiers.
Recover exact potion/food effects, stacking, durations, cooldowns, intermediate classes and concrete item definitions without inventing original values.
status: Design captured. Food exists as a class shell; complete non-equipment branches, potion effects and concrete definitions are not yet restored.
